title: Checkouts self-protect: effective ignore rule, doctor privacy integrity, docs
description:
## Parent

openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope — tasks 3.1–3.3, 4.2–4.3 (proposal approved, Ro5-revised). Fourth of 4 tracer-bullet slices; final gate for the change.

## What to build

Every checkout self-heals and self-reports: `turu init`/`turu sync` ensure `.whisper/private/` is *effectively* ignored (append the rule to root `.gitignore` only when `git check-ignore` does not already report the path; never duplicate; never touch other entries), and `turu doctor` runs three privacy checks — (a) effective ignore via `git check-ignore` (warning + fix hint), (b) no tracked files under `private/` via `git ls-files` (prominent failure: history cannot be retracted), (c) advisory leak-shape lint on public repo-local knowledge files (machine paths, hostnames, token-shaped strings) via envelope `warnings[]`. README + whisper skill pack document the transport decision, "git history is forever — prevention only" verbatim, and the `--global` fallback for read-only checkouts. `just ci` green closes the change's final task.

**Context:** Gitignore is the backstop, turu is the guarantee; doctor owns the hard guarantee. Ref: openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope/specs/workspace-maintenance/spec.md (ADDED ×2), tasks 4.2–4.3.

**Files / Systems:**
- `src/workspace.rs` (init/sync ignore-rule self-healing)
- `src/doctor.rs` (three privacy checks)
- `src/skill_pack.rs` (skill pack docs refresh, content-hashed)
- `README.md`
- `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/lifecycle.rs` (integration)

## Verifiable Value Claim

**Must (hard gate):** ≥7 new red/green tests green: init adds the rule exactly once and is idempotent (re-init changes nothing); rule covered by a nested `.gitignore` still counts as effectively ignored (no duplicate append); doctor warns when the path is not effectively ignored; doctor fails prominently on a tracked file under `private/` (fixture: `git add -f`); doctor emits advisory leak warnings and still exits 0.
**Meter:** `just ci 2>&1 | tail -2` — exit 0 (fmt + clippy -D warnings + test + build-locked)
**Baseline:** 105 tests green at 8011f5a; suite grows through slices 1–3
**Regression suite:** `just ci`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Fresh `turu init` in a checkout without the rule appends `.whisper/private/` to root `.gitignore` exactly once; re-init is a no-op
- [ ] Path covered by a nested ignore rule is NOT re-appended (effective-ignore truth, not text presence)
- [ ] `turu doctor` check (b) fails prominently when `git ls-files .whisper/private/` is non-empty, stating prevention cannot be retroactive
- [ ] Leak-shape lint is advisory: warnings in envelope, exit 0, no file modified
- [ ] Doctor pass-count tests updated for the new checks (known shift, cf. t6j gotcha) without weakening existing assertions
- [ ] README + skill pack state: transport decision, "git history is forever — prevention only", `--global` fallback for read-only checkouts
- [ ] `just ci` green — final task of openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope/tasks.md checked off
- [ ] File-header criterion: changed files update their Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale header (see file-headers)

## Blocked by

- whisper-eiy (doctor checks reference the private zone; leak lint needs the repo-local root from slice 1)

---
**CRITICAL: Follow Test Driven Development and Tidy First workflows.**
- Write tests *before* writing implementation code. Clean up related code *before* adding new functionality.

**Anti-goals (do NOT):**
- Modify, disable, or delete existing tests to make the suite pass (updating the doctor pass-count for added checks is expected and allowed; deleting assertions is not)
- Add new dependencies or modify lockfiles
- Make any privacy check blocking (leak lint is advisory by design; only the tracked-files check is a prominent failure)

title: Bundles and consolidation can never carry or touch the private zone
description:
## Parent

openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope — tasks 2.3–2.6 (proposal approved, Ro5-revised). Third of 4 tracer-bullet slices.

## What to build

The private zone becomes mechanically unreachable by transport and migration: `turu bundle pack` excludes everything under `.whisper/private/` and *refuses* (clear error, no bundle) any scope resolving there; `turu bundle unpack` never creates or modifies files under `private/` and places entries at paths resolved under current rules (legacy bundles unpack into the repo-local root); `consolidate` is bound by a regression guard — legacy-variant detection operates only on the workspace root, no checkout path is ever an input to a move/merge.

**Context:** "Detection that warns can be loose; anything that moves or publishes data cannot." Ref: openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope/specs/shared-store/spec.md (ADDED "Bundles never carry the private zone"), specs/workspace-routing/spec.md (consolidate guard scenario).

**Files / Systems:**
- `src/bundle.rs` (pack exclusion + refusal, unpack placement + write-refusal)
- `src/workspace.rs` (consolidate guard)
- `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/lifecycle.rs` (integration)

## Verifiable Value Claim

**Must (hard gate):** ≥6 new red/green tests green covering: pack excludes `private/` subtree and reports excluded count; pack refuses a private-resolved scope with no bundle produced; unpack skips entries targeting `private/` (reported in envelope); legacy bundle unpacks into repo-local root; consolidate guard (no checkout path selectable).
**Meter:** `just test 2>&1 | tail -2` — exit 0 with the new tests present
**Baseline:** suite green after slice 2 (whisper-eiy)
**Regression suite:** `just ci`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `turu bundle pack branch` in a checkout with private entries: bundle contains no path under `.whisper/private/`, envelope reports excluded count
- [ ] Packing a scope resolving under `private/` fails with a clear error and produces no bundle
- [ ] `turu bundle unpack` never writes into `private/`; pre-change bundles unpack into the repo-local root
- [ ] Consolidate guard: no checkout path (incl. `private/`) is ever moved or merged
- [ ] Automated tests cover the slice end-to-end
- [ ] File-header criterion: changed files update their Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale header (see file-headers)

## Blocked by

- whisper-eiy (the private zone must exist before it can be excluded)

---
**CRITICAL: Follow Test Driven Development and Tidy First workflows.**
- Write tests *before* writing implementation code. Clean up related code *before* adding new functionality.

**Anti-goals (do NOT):**
- Modify, disable, or delete existing tests to make the suite pass
- Add new dependencies or modify lockfiles
- Weaken or remove the exact-path rule (a nested `private/` must NOT inherit the guarantee)

title: Machine-private knowledge is readable locally but never pushed (.whisper/private/)
description:
## Parent

openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope — tasks 2.1–2.2 (proposal approved, Ro5-revised). Second of 4 tracer-bullet slices.

## What to build

Machine-specific or personal knowledge in a repo workspace has a canonical home that is structurally unpushable: `turu append --private` routes into `.whisper/private/` mirroring the repo-local layout (`private/env.md`, `private/branches/<slug>/notes.md`), and `turu recall` serves private entries alongside repo-local ones — included locally, excluded from every publication/transport verb by exact top-level path (exclusion itself is slice 3).

**Context:** Privacy as a structural exclusion zone — the boundary is a path, not a policy; no verb ever needs to judge. Ref: openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope/specs/workspace-routing/spec.md (ADDED "Private zone is read-included and publish-excluded").

**Files / Systems:**
- `src/workspace.rs` (private-zone routing, resolve surface)
- `src/recall.rs` (private zone in composition)
- `src/main.rs` (`--private` flag on append/resolve)
- `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/lifecycle.rs` (integration)

## Verifiable Value Claim

**Must (hard gate):** ≥4 new red/green tests green covering: `--private` append lands in `private/` mirroring layout; recall serves private entries (composition includes them); a `private/` dir nested deeper under `.whisper/` is NOT treated as the zone (exact-path rule).
**Meter:** `just test 2>&1 | tail -2` — exit 0 with the new tests present
**Baseline:** suite green after slice 1 (whisper-6fv)
**Regression suite:** `just ci`

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `turu append branch --private --text ...` on `main` writes `.whisper/private/branches/main/notes.md`
- [ ] `turu recall branch` on `main` serves entries from the private zone
- [ ] Exclusion is exact-path only: `.whisper/branches/x/private/` is ordinary content
- [ ] Automated tests cover the slice end-to-end
- [ ] File-header criterion: changed files update their Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale header (see file-headers)

## Blocked by

- whisper-6fv (repo-local root must exist for the private zone to mirror)

---
**CRITICAL: Follow Test Driven Development and Tidy First workflows.**
- Write tests *before* writing implementation code. Clean up related code *before* adding new functionality.

**Anti-goals (do NOT):**
- Modify, disable, or delete existing tests to make the suite pass
- Add new dependencies or modify lockfiles
- Implement publication-verb exclusion here (that is slice 3, whisper-TBD) — this slice is routing + read-inclusion only
notes: Anti-goal clarification: publication-verb exclusion (pack/unpack/consolidate) is implemented in whisper-4xo, not this ticket.

title: Repo/branch knowledge resolves, appends, and recalls from the checkout
description:
## Parent

openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope — tasks 1.1–1.3, 4.1 (proposal approved, Ro5-revised). Tracker: this is the first of 4 tracer-bullet slices.

## What to build

An agent appending branch notes in a checkout writes into the checkout's own `.whisper/`, commits it, and the notes are servable on any clone: `repo`/`branch` scopes resolve into the repo-local root (`.whisper/env.md`, `.whisper/branches/<slug>/notes.md`), `turu append` lands there by default with `--global` as escape hatch, and `turu recall` composes the repo-local root (incl. private zone) + workspace root in **store-major order**. The managed block regenerated by `turu sync` shows the new routing table.

**Context:** Decision A of the transport fork: transport is the repo's own git. Ref: openspec/changes/add-repo-private-scope/specs/workspace-routing/spec.md (MODIFIED "Scope resolution is exact and total", ADDED "Recall composes ... in store-major order").

**Precondition (do first, one command):** `openspec archive add-shared-bundle --yes` so the `shared-store` spec lands in `specs/` before implementation starts.

**Files / Systems:**
- `src/workspace.rs` (resolution, init, managed-block template)
- `src/recall.rs` (store-major composition, id dedup)
- `src/main.rs` (CLI: default destinations, `--global` flag)
- `tests/cli.rs`, `tests/lifecycle.rs` (integration)

## Verifiable Value Claim

**Must (hard gate):** ≥8 new red/green tests green covering: resolve repo/branch → repo-local paths; append default + `--global` escape; recall store-major composition including the interleaving case (a newer workspace-root entry still serves *after* older repo-local entries); id dedup across stores; managed block lists repo-local destinations.
**Meter:** `just test 2>&1 | tail -2` — exit 0 with the new tests present
**Baseline:** 105 tests green (`just ci` at 8011f5a)
**Regression suite:** `just ci` (fmt + clippy -D warnings + test + build-locked)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `turu resolve branch` in a checkout returns `<repo-root>/.whisper/branches/<slug>/notes.md`; `global`/`group`/`worktree` scopes unchanged
- [ ] `turu append branch` writes repo-local; `turu append branch --global` writes workspace root
- [ ] `turu recall repo` serves repo-local entries before workspace-root entries, recency-ranked within each store, no entry twice
- [ ] `turu sync` managed block shows the repo-local routing table
- [ ] Automated tests cover the slice end-to-end
- [ ] File-header criterion: changed files update their Purpose/Responsibilities/Rationale header (see file-headers)

## Blocked by

None - can start immediately (after the archive precondition above)

---
**CRITICAL: Follow Test Driven Development and Tidy First workflows.**
- Write tests *before* writing implementation code. Clean up related code *before* adding new functionality.

**Anti-goals (do NOT):**
- Modify, disable, or delete existing tests to make the suite pass
- Add new dependencies or modify lockfiles
- Change the scope enum or the canonical repo-key derivation (pure function of remote URL)
close_reason: Shipped 8a83802: repo-local routing (tasks 1.1-1.3, 4.1). 116 tests green (12 new), just ci green, dogfooded in this repo. Next: whisper-eiy (private zone).

title: turu recall usage telemetry for staleness signals
description: Port the core insight from hermes-agent's curator: self-improvement without usage tracking is a landfill. turu recall should track per-entry use_count and last_recalled (O_APPEND sidecar or in-entry fields updated on recall reads). Surface as doctor/distill signal: doctor flags entries never recalled or stale beyond a threshold; distill --begin includes recency so the rewrite pass can prune/collapse dead entries.
acceptance_criteria: recall updates usage fields idempotently; doctor gains a staleness check with fix hint; distill begin exposes recency; all under TDD, no LLM in path
notes: Rule-of-5 design verdict (NEEDS_REVISION before claim): (1) storage = append-only, machine-local usage sidecar keyed by entry id — in-entry fields would break the O_APPEND fast path, distill snapshot hashing, and bundle determinism; excluded from bundle pack/unpack. (2) recall stays a pure read; usage records written via O_APPEND appends, --no-usage escape for read-only contexts. (3) distill re-statements orphan old-id usage records — orphaned usage ignored, never a doctor warning. (4) usage counts only entries actually served within budget (filtered/budget-skipped ≠ used). (5) quantified gates: doctor warns at last_recalled > 90d, or use_count==0 with entry age > 30d (never-used grace floor). Anti-goal: no gaming surface — usage only from recall serving.

title: Wire feedback subcommand via genesis::feedback
description: whisper depends on genesis (guide only) but has no feedback subcommand. Wire it using the pretender pattern: clap subcommand delegating to genesis::feedback::handle_feedback with tool name/version/repo. Include a genesis compatibility test like vampiro's genesis_compatibility.rs. Refs: genesis src/feedback.rs doc example; existing integrations in wai, dont, espectacular, pretender, vampiro.

title: warn when repo-private workspace_root shadows global scope
description: A repo-private workspace_root intentionally beats everything in load() (config.rs), which also shadows the global scope (rules.md) for that repo — a repo can lose sight of global rules with no warning. GH issue #1 follow-up: add a docs note and/or a turu check/turu doctor warning when a repo-private root is set and the global rules.md diverges from the shadowed one.

title: fix: anchor relative repo workspace_root to config dir, not cwd
description: Repo-private .whisper/config.toml with relative workspace_root resolves against process cwd instead of the dir containing the config. find_repo_config() discards the config dir in load(); expand_tilde passes relative paths through unanchored. Running turu from a subdir silently creates a stray workspace tree (split-brain notes). GH issue #1. Fix: anchor relative repo workspace_root to the config dir; red test per repo TDD convention.

title: Decide shared-bundle transport (in-repo dir vs git-refs vs remote)
description: Strategic fork documented in openspec/changes/add-shared-bundle/design.md — deliberately deferred until real multi-machine/team usage exists. The bundle primitive (deterministic pack/unpack, shipped in v0.4.0) is the common substrate all three options consume. Options: A) committed .whisper/ dir in-repo (zero transport, PR noise), B) bundles under git refs on the existing remote (beads-style, no working-tree noise), C) central remote store (violates ownership maxim, infra to run). Decide when a second machine/team actually needs shared knowledge.
close_reason: Decision made: option A (in-repo .whisper/ with deterministic private zone .whisper/private/, gitignored). Scaffolded as openspec change add-repo-private-scope (proposal/design/3 spec deltas/15 tasks), validated strict. Implementation tickets whisper-6fv -> whisper-eiy -> {whisper-4xo, whisper-7eo} filed with base_commit 8011f5a.

title: Add ci.yml workflow (repo has no CI — only release.yml added)
Implement whisper consolidate — migrate legacy repo-key dirs to canonical key
description: Per the skill's '/w consolidate' mode: detect legacy repo-key directory variants (bare name, owner-only, alias-host with colon) under repos/ and migrate their contents into the canonical key directory. Detection already exists in workspace::legacy_variants.

title: Add whisper doctor via genesis::doctor module
description: Deep workspace diagnostics: layout integrity, group definition consistency, orphaned branch/worktree slots, permission checks. Use genesis doctor module conventions shared across the suite.
close_reason: Implementing now: turu doctor via genesis DoctorReport.

title: Update incitaciones whisper skill to delegate mechanical steps to whisper CLI
description: Replace shell-snippet procedures in content/distilled/whisper/ (repo key derivation, branch slugs, worktree slots, scope routing) with whisper CLI invocations: whisper key / resolve / append / status / check. Keep manual fallbacks when the binary is absent. Update references/*.md accordingly.
close_reason: Done: whisper skill now ships from this repo via 'turu skill install' (skill_pack pattern, 11 files, content-hashed, staleness via turu doctor). Incitaciones converted to a thin pointer (charly-vibes/incitaciones) — manual references/ kept as fallback.

title: Register whisper with ddl + homebrew-charly/scoop-charly
description: Tool is built (v0.1.0) but not yet wired into the charly-vibes distribution: add to ddl's tool manifest, verify 'ddl install whisper' and 'ddl status' detect it, add cask/formula to homebrew-charly and scoop-charly.
close_reason: Filed as DDL issue in dulce-de-leche; closing this mirror.

title: advisory lint on append/distill-begin for incident-log-shaped entries
description: Hermes' skill linter flags 'incident-log-shape' — bodies dense in PR/issue numbers, dates, quoted chat — enforcing 'lessons, not logs': a pitfall is a generalizable rule plus one clause of why. Our branch notes.md is already drifting toward dated narration. Add an advisory lint to turu append and turu distill --begin: warn (never block) when text is dense in timestamps/ids/narration markers, suggesting the generalized form. Matches existing pattern: detection that warns can be loose (see consolidate's colon-rule lesson).
acceptance_criteria: lint heuristic with tests covering warn/pass cases; wired into append output envelope as warnings[] and distill begin output; advisory only — exit code and write behavior unchanged
notes: Rule-of-5 quantified heuristic: ≥3 date-like or id-like tokens per 500 chars ⇒ warning (tunable). Advisory only — exit code and write behavior unchanged; provenance: hermes-agent curator incident-log-shape lint + branch note 3b2c0f97 (self-improvement comparison). Sequence after whisper-t6j (both touch distill --begin output shape).
